rows.question: Is a gift of a house to my daughter valid if it is only written on plain paper, and does it need registration?
queries: Is a gift of a house to my daughter valid if it is only written on plain paper, and does it need registration?
gift of immovable property transfer of property instrument registered plain paper
Transfer of Property Act section 122 gift definition and section 123 transfer how effected
Registration Act section 17 documents of which registration is compulsory
topSources: The Transfer of Property Act, 1882 s122
The Registration Act, 1908 s17
The Transfer of Property Act, 1882 s123
The Societies Registration Act, 1860 s17
The Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969 s17
rows.answer:
A gift of immovable property such as a house cannot be effected by a writing on plain paper, and it must be registered [3]. For the purpose of making a gift of immovable property, the transfer must be effected by a registered instrument signed by or on behalf of the donor and attested by at least two witnesses, as required by Section 123 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 [3]. Additionally, instruments of gift of immovable property must be registered under Section 17 of the Registration Act, 1908 [2]. 

Regarding the Supreme Court judgment excerpt provided, in the case of "PHOOL PATTI AND ANR. versus RAM SINGH (DEAD) THROUGH LRS. & ANR." [2015] 1 S.C.R. 305, the Supreme Court noted a contention that a transaction amounting to a gift of agricultural land and a residential house could only be through a written instrument that was duly stamped and registered, and if it was neither written, nor stamped, nor registered, it could not be acted upon [13].

rows.answer:
Under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, whoever commits rape, except in the cases provided for in sub-section (2), shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than ten years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine [1].

In cases where a person commits rape under sub-section (2) of Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (such as by certain public servants, members of armed forces, persons in a position of authority, or during communal violence, among other specified circumstances), the punishment is rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than ten years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person's natural life, and also liability to fine [1].

Whoever commits rape on a woman under sixteen years of age, under sub-section (3) of Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than twenty years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person's natural lif

rows.answer:
Under the old Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, every information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence, if given orally to an officer in charge of a police station, had to be reduced to writing by him or under his direction, and read over to the informant [1][7]. Every such information, whether given in writing or reduced to writing, was required to be signed by the person giving it, and its substance had to be entered in a book kept by the officer in the form prescribed by the State Government [1][7]. This is covered now by Section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 [2].

Related provisions:
- Section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, which covers "Information in cognizable cases" [2].
- Section 154 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, which covers "Information in cognizable cases" [1][7].
- Section 174 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, which covers "Information as to non-cognizable cases and investigation of such cases" [3].
- Section 175 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, which covers "Police officer's power to investigate cognizable case" [8].

rows.answer:
Whoever causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine under Section 106 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 [1]. If such an act is done by a registered medical practitioner while performing a medical procedure, the punishment is imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, and also a fine under Section 106 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 [1]. Furthermore, whoever causes the death of any person by rash and negligent driving of a vehicle not amounting to culpable homicide, and escapes without reporting it to a police officer or a Magistrate soon after the incident, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine under Section 106 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 [1].

rows.answer:
Yes, where any senior citizen has transferred their property by way of gift or otherwise after the commencement of the Act, subject to the condition that the transferee shall provide basic amenities and basic physical needs to the transferor, and the transferee refuses or fails to provide such amenities and physical needs, the transfer of property shall be deemed to have been made by fraud, coercion, or undue influence, and shall, at the option of the transferor, be declared void by the Tribunal under Section 23 of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 [1]. As expounded by the Supreme Court in Urmila Dixit versus Sunil Sharan Dixit and Ors., the two conditions for attracting Section 23(1) are that the transfer must have been made subject to the condition that the transferee shall provide the basic amenities and basic physical needs to the transferor, and that the transferee refuses or fails to provide them [11].
